name: Working with very few parameters
gist: Lightweight models that run fast and need little memory—from linear regressions to pruned networks—for when data is scarce or compute is tight.
explain: Neural networks have millions or billions of internal weights—numbers that determine how the network transforms input to output—and training them takes compute and data. But many practical sequence problems have tight constraints. An embedded device on a sensor has limited memory. A manufacturer needs predictions in milliseconds, not seconds. A startup has only weeks of data on a new product. In these cases, you cannot use a massive model. The question becomes: how good a forecaster can you build with minimal capacity? Sometimes this means going back to classics—linear regression, exponential smoothing, autoregressive models—which have few weights but strong mathematical foundations. Sometimes it means designing neural networks that are smaller or have special structure.

The trade-off is accuracy versus efficiency. A large model might forecast with 10 percent error, but a small model might have 15 percent error. For many applications, 15 percent error is good enough for decision-making, especially if the small model is 100 times faster or uses 100 times less memory because speed and resource efficiency matter when you are deploying to millions of devices or serving millions of users. The hidden challenge is that this trade-off is not smooth. A model with half the weights does not have exactly half the accuracy; sometimes it degrades sharply. So the research is about finding the sweet spot: the smallest model that still captures the key patterns in the sequence.

Papers in this area revisit statistical methods—like linear regression, exponential smoothing, and vector autoregression—and ask whether they can be competitive with neural methods in settings where data is limited and compute matters. Some propose hybrid approaches, combining a fast linear model for the trend with a small neural network for residuals. Others design efficient architectures: convolutional nets with fewer layers, or mechanisms that only look at a small window of past values instead of the entire history. Pruning is another technique—train a larger model, then remove connections or weights that do not contribute much, leaving a smaller model. The theme is pragmatism: accuracy is not the only metric that matters.

papers.title: Bilinear Bandits with Partially Observable Features
papers.contribution: BiRoLF achieves Õ(√((dx+dhx)(dy+dhy)T)) regret bound where dx,dy are observable dimensions and dhx,dhy denote effective orthogonal-complement dimensions.

papers.title: Efficient Neural Controlled Differential Equations via Attentive Kernel Smoothing
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy while significantly reducing Number of Function Evaluations and total inference time compared to spline-based baselines.

papers.title: Learning Mixtures of Linear Dynamical Systems (MoLDS) via Hybrid Tensor–EM Method
papers.contribution: Hybrid approach provides identifiability guarantees while combining global initialization robustness with flexible latent model fitting for mixtures of LDS.

papers.title: TSPulse: Tiny Pre-Trained Models with Disentangled Representations for Rapid Time-Series Analysis
papers.contribution: Despite compact size, achieves +20% on anomaly detection (rank-1 on TSB-AD), +25% in similarity search, +50% in imputation, and +5-16% in multivariate classification.

papers.title: Being More Lightweight and Practical: Mini-sized Contrastive Learning Pre-trained Models for Fine-grained Traffic Task
papers.contribution: The lightweight framework demonstrates superior performance on six fine-grained datasets while significantly reducing model parameters for practical deployment.

papers.title: Decoupling Universal Laws and Environmental Heterogeneity: A Physics-Inspired Framework for Robust Spatio-Temporal Forecasting
papers.contribution: Demonstrates consistent improvements across in-distribution forecasting, out-of-distribution generalization, few-shot cross-city transfer, and continual learning over state-of-the-art baselines.

papers.title: ParalESN: Enabling parallel information processing in Reservoir Computing
papers.contribution: Achieves competitive predictive accuracy with traditional RC and deep learning while delivering computational savings by orders of magnitude.

papers.title: Rethinking Time-Series Imputation as Conditional Inference along Temporal Evolution
papers.contribution: CBiT improves imputation accuracy by reducing Masked MAE by 27.3% and Masked RMSE by 18.6% across different missing rates.

papers.title: Revealing Scaling Paradox in Large-scale Time Series Models: Implications for More Efficient and Accurate Forecasting
papers.contribution: Retaining only 21% of parameters achieves up to 12% accuracy improvement and 2.7x inference speedup, with over 95% task improvements on 8 SOTA models.

papers.title: TRACE: Trajectory Recovery for Continuous Mechanism Evolution in Causal Representation Learning
papers.contribution: Recovers mixing trajectories with up to 0.99 correlation, substantially outperforming discrete-switching baselines and enabling discovery of intermediate mechanism states never observed during training.
